title: Rigidity of connected actions on groups of multiplicative type, including nonreduced groups
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ and $D$ be affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume $G$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], and $D$ is of multiplicative type, meaning that $D$ is isomorphic as an $F$-group scheme to $D(M)=\operatorname{Spec}F[M]$ for a finitely generated abelian group $M$, with comultiplication $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$ on the group-algebra basis. Let $a:G\times_F D\to D$ be an action by group-scheme automorphisms: for every commutative $F$-algebra $A$ and $g\in G(A)$, the map $d\mapsto a(g,d)$ is a group automorphism of $D(A)$, naturally under change of $A$. Then $a$ is the second projection; equivalently $a(g,d)=d$ for all $A,g,d$. No smoothness or connectedness of $D$ is assumed.

source.place: Corollary 12.37, printed p.244, following Theorem 12.36, pp.243--244. Applied to conjugation on a normal multiplicative-type subgroup this gives Corollary 12.38.

proof.text: Choose the group-scheme isomorphism $D\simeq D(M)$ in the hypothesis and conjugate the action by it. It suffices to prove the assertion for $D=\operatorname{Spec}F[M]$. Put $B=\Gamma(G,\mathcal O_G)$, so $G=\operatorname{Spec}B$ by affineness. The affine product formula identifies the coordinate ring of $G\times_F D$ with $B\otimes_F F[M]=B[M]$. The identification sends $b\otimes e_m$ to $be_m$; its inverse sends a finite sum $\sum_m b_me_m$ to $\sum_m b_m\otimes e_m$. Both preserve products by the tensor multiplication formula. The pullback of the action is therefore an $F$-algebra map $\alpha:F[M]\to B[M]$.

source.place: Corollary 12.37 and the coordinate construction of D(M), pp.230--232; affine product is Stacks Tag 01I4.

proof.text: Fix $m\in M$ and write $u=\alpha(e_m)$. Let $\Delta_B:B[M]\to B[M]\otimes_B B[M]$ send $e_v$ to $e_v\otimes e_v$, and let $\varepsilon_B:B[M]\to B$ send every $e_v$ to $1$. The homomorphism-in-the-second-variable hypothesis gives $\Delta_B(u)=u\otimes u$ and $\varepsilon_B(u)=1$. Explicitly, in the test $F$-algebra $B[M]\otimes_B B[M]$, take the $G$-point induced by $B$ and the two $D$-points induced by the two basis inclusions. The equality $a(g,d_1d_2)=a(g,d_1)a(g,d_2)$ evaluated on the character $e_m$ is the first formula. In the test algebra $B$, take the universal $G$-point and the identity of $D$; $a(g,1)=1$ gives the second. Thus these are identities of coordinate functions, including nilpotents.

source.place: Corollary 12.37, group-homomorphism hypothesis; Lemma 12.4, group-like equations, p.232.

proof.text: Write $u=\sum_{v\in S}b_ve_v$ with finite support, extending $b_v=0$ off $S$. The elements $e_v\otimes e_w$ form a $B$-basis of $B[M]\otimes_B B[M]$: expand both factors, and recover each coefficient by the $B$-bilinear map sending $(\sum x_ve_v,\sum y_we_w)$ to $x_vy_w$. Comparing these coefficients in the first equation of Step 2 gives $b_v^2=b_v$ and $b_vb_w=0$ for $v\ne w$. The counit equation gives $\sum_{v\in S}b_v=1$. This comparison uses only finite sums and holds for torsion in $M$ and for arbitrary nilpotents in $B$.

source.place: Lemma 12.4 and its proof, p.232; the orthogonal-idempotent calculation over B in place of the field.

proof.text:
For any coefficient $b_v$, the idempotent--clopen correspondence makes $D(b_v)$ open and closed in $\operatorname{Spec}B=G$. Connectedness implies $D(b_v)$ is empty or all of $G$. Uniqueness in that correspondence, together with $D(0)=\varnothing$ and $D(1)=G$, gives $b_v=0$ or $b_v=1$. The identity section supplies an $F$-algebra map $\eta:B	o F$, hence $0

source.place: Tag 00EE, lemma-disjoint-decomposition; Milne Lemma 12.4, replacing the field idempotent argument by connectedness.

proof.text: The action identity $a(1,d)=d$ says that $(\eta\otimes1)\alpha:F[M]\to F[M]$ is the identity. Applying it to $e_m$ in Step 4 gives $e_{\nu(m)}=e_m$, so independence of the specified group-algebra basis gives $\nu(m)=m$. Therefore $\alpha(e_m)=1\otimes e_m$ for every $m$. By $F$-linearity the same equality holds on all of $F[M]$. The affine spectrum correspondence makes $a$ the second projection, whose pullback is $e_m\mapsto1\otimes e_m$. Conjugating back proves the original assertion, and evaluating the equality on every commutative $F$-algebra proves the stated functor-of-points formula. No step assumes reducedness, smoothness, or connectedness of $D$.
